canvas-01-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 1 is the map drawn below the key map and street index, at 100 feet to an inch, covering the eastern edge of Hillsdale along Washington Avenue. Hillsdale Avenue runs along the top, cut by the border of the index panel, and Washington Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from the west edge to the south-east corner. Stockton runs down the west edge to Pascack Creek in the south-west corner, beyond which lies the Borough of Westwood. Between Hillsdale and Washington Avenues are Hopper Avenue and Holdrum Avenue, laid out with long lots that are mostly vacant; block 71 between them holds a ball diamond. East of Holdrum Avenue a row of frame dwellings faces a street ending at Lincoln Terrace. South of Washington Avenue lie large open tracts (blocks 69 and 208) with scattered dwellings, chicken houses, the Hillsdale Awning and Shade Company, and greenhouses near the south edge, and Wheelman Place (Whitman Place) runs south from Washington Avenue with a short row of houses. The heavy line in the upper right separates part 2, which shows the next stretch of Washington Avenue at a different angle. Water pipes, fire alarm boxes and lot and house numbers are drawn.
notes: Printed sheet 1; canvas label is Index. The upper half of the canvas is the key map and street index and is masked out.
Hopper Avenue and Holdrum Avenue are now Hopper Street and Holdrum Street; Stockton is Stockton Street; Wheelman Place (Whitman Place) is Whitman Place.
Hillsdale Avenue / Holdrum Street and Hillsdale Avenue / Stockton Street were hand-picked; the detector paired a lot line at Stockton (10 m off).
Hillsdale Awning and Shade Company; ball diamond on block 71; greenhouses.

Printed sheet 1. Top half is the key map (1000 ft to an inch), index and key, not georeferenced. Bottom half is map at 100 ft: two parts. Part 1 (left): Hillsdale Av, Washington Av, Stockton, Hopper Av, Holdrum Av, Lincoln Ter. Part 2 (right, behind heavy line, own north arrow turned about 40 deg): Washington Av, Hopkins Av, Demarest Av, Wheelman Pl. Part 1: 4 detected + 2 hand-picked (Hillsdale/Holdrum, Hillsdale/Stockton). Part 2: helmert on Hopkins St / Washington Av (detected) and Demarest Av / Washington Av (hand-picked), low confidence.

canvas-01-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 1 occupies the upper right of the map below the index, separated from part 1 by a heavy line, and is drawn at 100 feet to an inch turned about 30 degrees, with its own north arrow pointing to the upper left. It continues Washington Avenue eastward from part 1 to the edge of the borough at Demarest Avenue, which runs along the Hillsdale Township line with the Township of Riverdale beyond. Washington Avenue runs across the top of the part with a row of frame dwellings on both sides; Hopkins Avenue runs south from it, and a dash-dot match line marked A and B at the west end ties the part to the map below. South of Washington Avenue lie the large blocks 208 and 208 1/2, largely open, with dwellings along Demarest Avenue and a few along Hopkins Avenue, and block 208 1/4 east of Demarest Avenue. Water pipes, a fire alarm box and house numbers from about 430 to 470 are shown along Washington Avenue.
notes: Printed sheet 1, turned part; placed by one detected junction (Hopkins Street / Washington Avenue) and one hand-picked (Demarest Avenue / Washington Avenue), both on Washington Avenue: helmert, low confidence.
Hopkins Avenue is now Hopkins Street. This Demarest Avenue keeps its name; the Demarest Avenue of sheet 7 is now Liberty Avenue.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the business centre of Hillsdale at 50 feet to an inch, twice the scale of the other sheets. It is bounded by Orchard and Cross Streets at the top and Washington Avenue at the bottom, with Patterson at the left edge and Central Avenue at the right. The New York and New Jersey Railroad (Erie Line) runs diagonally across the sheet from top left to bottom right, with the Hillsdale Depot beside the tracks south of Hillsdale Avenue and a coal yard between the tracks and Washington Avenue. Between the railroad and Broadway (Summit Avenue) the block from Park Avenue to Hillsdale Avenue is an open park, and a smaller park strip lies south of Hillsdale Avenue. West of the railroad on Hillsdale Avenue stands a row of one-storey stores containing the post office, the Hillsdale Herald printing office and an insurance office, with a large garage, show room and repair shop on Park Avenue. Broadway is the commercial street: on its east side are brick stores and a bank at Park Avenue, a long block of concrete-block stores, auto stalls, and between Hillsdale and Washington Avenues a department store, a drug store, hardware storage, a bakery and a row of cinder-block stores. A batteries and vulcanizing shop stands at Broadway and Cross Street. The remainder of the sheet is frame dwellings with garages on deep lots. Six- and twelve-inch water pipes, house numbers and lot numbers are shown, and the adjoining sheets 3, 6 and 7 are noted at the margins.
notes: Drawn at 50 feet to an inch; the other map sheets are at 100 feet.
Broadway is labelled Broadway (Summit Avenue).
Hillsdale Depot of the New York and New Jersey Railroad (Erie Line), now the Pascack Valley Line; three grade crossings were rejected by the fit at 4.7 to 6.3 m.
Post office, Hillsdale Herald printing office, bank, department store and drug store.
Downtown at 50 ft: Broadway (Summit Av), Hillsdale Av, Park Av, Orchard, Cross, Central Av, Patterson, Washington Av, NY & NJ RR (Erie) and Hillsdale depot. One part.

sheet-3-1.description: The main part of sheet 3 covers the northern centre of Hillsdale at 100 feet to an inch, from Parkview Avenue and Clinton Avenue at the top down to Orchard and Cross at the bottom. In the upper left is the curving street plan of the Hillsdale Manor development west of the railroad: Lake Drive, Esplanade, The Circle, Mansion Place and Parkview Avenue, laid out in numbered lots with only a few dwellings built, bounded on the west by Pascack Creek. The New York and New Jersey Railroad (Erie Line) crosses the sheet from top to bottom with the Hillsdale Manor Depot at the top, and a long row of narrow lots lies between Lake Drive and the tracks. East of the railroad, Broadway (Summit Avenue) runs north-south; to its west a large open block (97) reaches from West Street to Brookside Place, and below it the blocks of Brookside Place, Piermont Avenue and Prospect Place are divided into narrow building lots with frame dwellings. Patterson runs beside the railroad at the bottom, with New, Valley and Orchard and the Hillsdale Laundry. East of Broadway are Clinton, Wilts, Knickerbocker and Piermont Avenues and Cross, with Loretto, Franklin and Central Avenue, part of the Hillsdale Manor Section; a public garage stands at Broadway and Piermont Avenue. Coal sheds of a coal and wood dealer stand on Patterson by the railroad. Water pipes, house numbers and block numbers are shown. The lower left corner is taken by an inset (part 2), and a strip of Pascack Creek and the Sheet 6 key number lie below it.
notes: Lake Drive is now Lake Street, Parkview Avenue is Parkview Drive, Esplanade is Esplanade Drive and Mansion Place is Manson Place.
Franklin is now Legion Place; Loretto is Loretta Street (Clinton Avenue / Loretta Street was rejected at 19.8 m, so Loretta Street does not follow the old Loretto line).
South and West are marked not opened.
Hillsdale Manor Depot on the New York and New Jersey Railroad (Erie Line); Hillsdale Laundry Inc. on New.

Hillsdale Manor south part and Patterson / Piermont area at 100 ft: Lake Drive, Esplanade, Parkview Av, The Circle, Mansion Pl, Broadway, Wilts, Clinton, Knickerbocker, Piermont, Prospect Pl, Brookside Pl, Patterson, Valley, New, Orchard, Cross, Central. Two parts: main, and inset lower left (Broadway at Cole's Crossing Rd, Hillsdale Manor Coal & Lumber, turned with its own north arrow). Part 2 (inset) has no modern junction: placed on the east end of modern Coles Crossing Road at the Pascack Valley Line plus a derived point at the atlas scale (north -11.4 deg); low confidence; its Broadway agrees with sheet 3 part 1 to about 5 m.

sheet-3-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 3 is an inset in the lower left corner, enclosed by a heavy border and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, turned about 11 degrees from the main map. It shows a stretch of Broadway north of the area of the main sheets, near the northern end of Hillsdale, where Cole's Crossing Road crosses the single track of the New York and New Jersey Railroad (Erie) and meets Broadway. Between the railroad and Broadway lies the yard of the Hillsdale Manor Coal and Lumber Corporation, with coal pockets on a siding, lumber sheds, a lumber storage building, storage buildings, an office with scales, a brick shed and oil tanks on iron stilts. An auto repair shop of concrete block stands at the corner of Broadway and Cole's Crossing Road, with gasoline tanks beside it. East of Broadway the inset shows only a few dwellings and a large open block (124); the block west of the railroad is numbered 123. House numbers along Broadway run from about 541 to 603. The south end of the inset shows Broadway bending slightly to the east.
notes: Placed by hand: one point where modern Coles Crossing Road ends at the Pascack Valley Line (the old grade crossing) and a derived point at the atlas scale; low confidence.
Hillsdale Manor Coal and Lumber Corporation yard with coal pockets on a siding of the New York and New Jersey Railroad (Erie).

Two parts: main, and inset lower left (Broadway at Cole's Crossing Rd, Hillsdale Manor Coal & Lumber, turned with its own north arrow). sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the Hillsdale Manor Section in the north-east of the borough at 100 feet to an inch. The upper half is a regular grid of long narrow blocks between St. Nicholas Avenue at the top, Clinton Avenue, Wilts Avenue and Knickerbocker Avenue, crossed by Loretto, Florence, Franklin, Vincent, Ferndale, Riverdale, Evergreen and Oakland, with William Road (Kinderkermack Road) along the east edge. The blocks are cut into numbered lots 25 feet wide, most of them still vacant; scattered frame dwellings, a few from plans, and the Lakeview Inn at the corner of Loretto and St. Nicholas Avenue are the main buildings, with an inn on Riverdale between Clinton and Knickerbocker Avenues. Below Knickerbocker Avenue a very large open block (112) reaches down to Piermont Avenue, with a row of lots (112A to 112D) along Knickerbocker and a row along Kinderkermack Road. The lower part of the sheet is more built up: Central Avenue, Bergen Avenue and Magnolia Avenue, running diagonally, lead down to Piermont, Conklin and Large Avenues and Cross, with frame dwellings and garages on most lots of blocks 88 to 92, a plumbing shop on block 104, and a short street labelled Stockton between Piermont and Large Avenues at the east edge. Water pipes, fire alarm boxes, house numbers and lot numbers are shown.
notes: Ferndale is now the northern part of Magnolia Avenue.
Franklin is now Legion Place; Loretto is Loretta Street; Florence, Vincent, Riverdale, Evergreen and Oakland are now Streets.
William (Kinderkermack Road) at the east edge and Stockton between Piermont and Large Avenues are both on the line of modern Kinderkamack Road.
Knickerbocker Avenue / Vincent Street (11.4 m) and Clinton Avenue / Oakland Street (13.3 m) were rejected by the fit.
Lakeview Inn at Loretto and St. Nicholas Avenue.

Hillsdale Manor section at 100 ft: St Nicholas, Clinton, Wilts, Knickerbocker, Piermont, Conklin, Large Avs; Loretto, Florence, Franklin, Vincent, Ferndale, Riverdale, Evergreen, Oakland, William Rd (Kinderkermack Rd), Central, Bergen, Magnolia, Stockton. One part. Old Ferndale is now Magnolia Avenue, Franklin is Legion Place, William Rd and Stockton are Kinderkamack Road.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the western residential district of Hillsdale south of Hillsdale Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Hillsdale Avenue runs across the upper part of the sheet; north of it the ground is mostly open (block 201) with a few dwellings and outbuildings. South of Hillsdale Avenue is a grid of long blocks divided into narrow numbered lots: Maple Avenue, Fernwood Avenue and Oakwood Avenue run east-west, crossed by Chestnut, Colonial Boulevard, Beach, Elm, Oak and Taylor, with Cedar and Summit further east. In the south centre, Vorrath Place, Hering Place and Cottage Place are short streets of small lots east of Beach, and a group of very long lots (block 31) lies between Elm and Taylor. In the south-east, Boulevard North and Boulevard South run east to Summit with blocks 35 and 36 laid out in lots. Most lots are vacant; frame dwellings with garages are spread thinly, more densely along Maple Avenue and Colonial Boulevard. A cement block manufacturing plant stands on block 33 between Taylor and Cedar. The boundary between Hillsdale Township and Washington Township, drawn as a dash-dot line, crosses the lower part of the sheet diagonally, and the south-west corner (blocks 202 to 206) lies in Washington Township. Van Place is a short stub at the west edge. Water pipes, fire alarm boxes and house numbers are shown, and sheet 6 adjoins on the east.
notes: Beach is now Beech Street; Chestnut, Oak, Taylor and Cedar are now Streets.
Boulevard North is now Crest Road (from its position); Summit is Summit Drive.
Chestnut Street / Maple Avenue was rejected by the fit at 13.5 m.
Cement block manufacturing plant between Taylor and Cedar.
The Hillsdale Township / Washington Township line crosses the sheet.

West side at 100 ft: Hillsdale Av, Maple Av, Fernwood Av, Oakwood Av, Vorrath Pl, Hering Pl, Cottage Pl, Boulevard N and S; Chestnut, Colonial Blvd, Beach, Elm, Oak, Taylor, Cedar, Summit. Hillsdale / Washington Township line crosses the south. One part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the south-western part of Hillsdale at 100 feet to an inch, from Orchard and Hillsdale Avenue at the top to the boundary with the Borough of Westwood, which crosses the sheet as a dash-dot line just below Beechwood Drive. Pascack Creek winds through the sheet from the top centre, under Hillsdale Avenue and a concrete bridge, and loops around the south-east corner. The centre of the sheet is a planned development of small lots lettered Glen Brook Park, between Yesler Way and Glenwood Avenue, with Hazelwood Avenue and Sycamore Avenue crossed by Glendale Drive, Center Drive and Beechwood Drive, and Riverside Drive running diagonally along the creek; it is partly built with frame dwellings. West of Yesler Way are Maple Avenue, Boulevard North, Summit Street and Boulevard South with large open blocks, and Yesler Way continues south past Harding Avenue into Westwood. In the north are Valley (not open), Orchard, Patterson and Park Avenue, with the Church of St. John (Roman Catholic) on Hillsdale Avenue by the creek. In the north-east corner Washington Avenue meets Broadway (Summit Avenue) at the New York and New Jersey Railroad (Erie Lines), where a round house of two stalls with a turntable, railroad supply houses, an oil house and a hay house stand in the railroad yard. A strip of narrow lots on Brookside Walk and Brook Place occupies the east edge beside the creek. Water pipes, fire alarm boxes and house numbers are shown.
notes: Glenwood Avenue is now Lafayette Avenue.
Yesler Way south of Beechwood Drive is now Hillside Avenue; Harding Avenue meets it there.
Boulevard North is now Crest Road; Summit Street is Summit Drive.
Valley is marked not open.
Church of St. John (Roman Catholic) on Hillsdale Avenue; railroad round house of 2 stalls with turntable on the New York and New Jersey Railroad (Erie Lines).

South-west at 100 ft: Hillsdale Av, Maple Av, Yesler Way, Hazelwood Av, Sycamore Av, Glenwood Av, Glendale Dr, Center Dr, Beechwood Dr, Riverside Dr, Harding Av, Brookside Walk, Brook Pl, Pascack Creek, Erie round house. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the south-eastern part of the borough of Hillsdale, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It runs from Large Avenue and Cross Street at the top down to Pascack Creek, which forms the boundary with the Borough of Westwood along the bottom of the sheet, and from Broadway (Summit Avenue) and the New York and New Jersey Railroad (Erie Line) on the west to Stockton and Kinderkermack Road on the east. The streets are Large, Cross, Demarest, Park, Hillsdale and Washington Avenues, Harrington and Lawrence running east-west, crossed by Central Avenue, Valley, George Place, Magnolia Avenue, Trinity Place, Grove, Kinderkermack Road (Grove), Allwood Place, Stockton and Fairview Avenue, with Kinderkermack Road running diagonally across the north-east corner. The area is mostly frame dwellings on regular lots with outbuildings. Public buildings are grouped around Hillsdale Avenue and Magnolia Avenue: the Town Hall and Fire Department on Park Avenue near Central Avenue, Hillsdale School No. 1 and the Hillsdale School Annex between Demarest and Hillsdale Avenues, a hall, Trinity Protestant Episcopal Church, and the Hillsdale Methodist Episcopal Church on Hillsdale Avenue. Small commercial and garage buildings stand on Washington Avenue east of Magnolia Avenue, and an auto repair shop and filling station sit at the corner of Broadway and Washington Avenue next to the railroad. Six-inch water pipes are drawn along most streets. The south-west corner shows the ends of Brookside Walk and Brook Place, which continue on sheet 6, and the creek is drawn crossing the railroad and Fairview Avenue on bridges.
notes: Demarest Avenue on this sheet is now Liberty Avenue.
Kinderkermack Road (Grove) south of Hillsdale Avenue and the diagonal Kinderkermack Road north of it are now both Kinderkamack Road; Grove north of Hillsdale Avenue is Grove Street.
Harrington is now Harrington Street; Lawrence is Lawrence Street.
Broadway is labelled Broadway (Summit Avenue).
Town Hall and Fire Department on Park Avenue; Hillsdale School No. 1 and Annex; Trinity Protestant Episcopal Church; Hillsdale Methodist Episcopal Church.

South-east at 100 ft: Large, Cross, Demarest, Park, Hillsdale, Washington, Harrington, Lawrence Avs; Central, Valley, George Pl, Magnolia, Trinity Pl, Grove, Kinderkermack Rd, Stockton, Allwood Pl, Fairview Av, Broadway; Pascack Creek. One part. Old Demarest Av is now Liberty Avenue.
